done_when: After a plan's latest read round passed, edits only below '## For the builders' need no new read (as they need no new approval): forge next, approval and task start accept them. An edit to the top part (title down to For the builders) still needs a round, and that round's prompt asks the reader to check only the diff and the sections it touches. Command-level tests: a builders-only edit after a pass (no round needed), a top-part edit after a pass (round needed, prompt names the diff and touched sections).

findings.body: The coordinator's ruling requires the pull-request check to accept the same edits as task start, but this changed entry point has no command-level regression test. The new test ends after `forge task start` (`tests/test_builders_edits_need_no_new_read.py:42`). Existing PR coverage at `tests/test_readloop_gates.py:154–163` exercises a document without the builders divider and expects rejection. Reverting this call to its old strict form would therefore leave those tests passing while builders-only edits still block merging. Add a test through `forge hook pr-check` with a committed builders-only edit after a passing round and verify that the document gate accepts it.
findings.title: Not done: command test for forge-pr-check accepting builders-only edits after a passing read

why: After a plan read passes, any later edit, even a one-line wording change, costs a full new read round of about ten minutes before the plan can be approved or its next task started
